source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.

gens.text: At terminal security within bustling corridors, queues wind around barriers where belongings divest into trays. Officers guide through scanners and metal detectors; some are singled out for a pat-down by another officer with a wand and a demand to remove outerwear. Documents flash under scrutiny; instructions and signs dictate the flow, courtesy is offered in measured tones—every gesture a note of control. Travelers navigate the process with patience, each step marked by an exchange that reflects the system's watchful eye. A traveler, singled out, follows instructions silently, placing possessions into trays while waiting for clearance from security personnel who assess belongings meticulously before allowing further passage. The officer gestures towards a screen and a pat-down area; another traveller is selected, documents are checked, and a wand sweeps across their body with methodical care, ensuring no prohibited items are concealed. Each action at the checkpoint serves as a silent acknowledgment of authority's reach, reinforcing the security apparatus’s vigilance against threats. Patience meets protocol, and compliance signals readiness to proceed. Travelers move through this register of control under the watchful gaze of security measures in place.

At the bustling checkpoint near customs, a long queue formed beside towering barriers; passengers divested their belongings into waiting trays. A sophisticated scanner whirred alongside a metal detector, while another officer motioned for an individual to step aside for further inspection. The traveler, singled out by his name flashing on a digital screen, handed over his documents with a nod to the official's impersonal yet courteous inquiry about the origin of a small electronic device found in his carry-on. Following this, an officer guided him towards another station for a thorough pat-down using a handheld wand, each gesture meticulous and routine under the watchful eye of security cameras. As he moved through these prescribed steps, the traveler noted the precise instructions posted on every wall, reinforcing the systematic and unyielding nature of airport security protocols—this journey would proceed only after passing through each phase of scrutiny with unwavering compliance. Beyond the pat-down area lay a final checkpoint where another officer reviewed his documentation once more before granting passage; here too, the atmosphere was marked by an air of controlled efficiency and purposeful anonymity. As the traveler finally emerged from this regulated environment, he realized that every detail—from the initial queue to the final review—had been choreographed to maintain order and ensure safety in a world where trust and verification were constant companions.
